title: Keyboard traversal and semantic roles for interactive tables; VPAT annex for dynamic tokens
creator: Elena Park
description:
Summary:
Improve keyboard traversal and semantic role mapping for the interactive table family (data-grid, editable rows, inline cell editors) with a targeted set of token contrast validations across dynamic theme modes. Compile a VPAT annex documenting the implementation decisions, test evidence, and remediation notes for dynamic tokens and keyboard/ARIA behaviors.

Background:
We continue to find edge cases where keyboard focus escapes expected order when inline editors or contextual action menus open, and where screen reader announcements vary between light/dark/high-contrast themes because token values are swapped at runtime. Previous audits surfaced token contrast regression risks during theme switches and inconsistent use of role="grid" vs role="table" in complex widgets. This ticket scopes a combined design + implementation approach to stabilize semantics, keyboard patterns, and VPAT evidence for auditors.

Scope (design + engineering collaboration):
- Define canonical keyboard traversal for all interactive table states (row select, cell edit, cell action menu, bulk action toolbar) and document in the component spec.
- Standardize semantic roles and ARIA attributes across table variants (role, aria-rowindex, aria-colindex, aria-level for nested rows, aria-live regions for cell-level validation).
- Surface token contrast pass/fail examples for light, dark, and high-contrast themes; provide recommended token mappings when tokens are dynamically swapped at runtime.
- Produce a VPAT annex that: enumerates the table components covered, lists test scenarios and results, links to audit artifacts (screen reader recordings, automated axe snapshots), and records design decisions for future audits.
- Provide design tokens guidance and implementation notes for engineers (variants to avoid, acceptable contrast deltas, and suggested fallback tokens).

Proposed solution:
1) Design: updated interaction matrix and flow diagrams for keyboard sequences; annotated Figma examples for focused, editing, and error states; token table for theme variants.
2) Engineering: component changes to centralize focus management (focus-trap layers for inline editors), explicit setAttribute calls for aria-rowindex/aria-colindex during virtualization, and a lightweight aria-live queue for validation messages to avoid noisy announcements.
3) Verification & VPAT: automated axe snapshots for each theme and state, 3 screen reader walkthroughs (NVDA+IE11 fallback, VoiceOver macOS, JAWS), and recorded videos linked in the annex.

Acceptance criteria:
- Design spec and Figma examples are approved by accessibility reviewer and UX lead.
- Keyboard traversal flows match the documented matrix in 95% of tested scenarios across supported browsers.
- All token contrast checks pass WCAG AA for normal text in light/dark and meet at least AA large-text in high-contrast mode; exceptions documented with compensating controls.
- VPAT annex is complete with evidence links, passes internal accessibility review, and is export-ready for enterprise compliance teams.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: design spec and token table (sprint 1).
- Phase 2: engineering implementation on a feature branch with CI checks for axe snapshots (sprint 2).
- Phase 3: accessibility review, fix cycle, and merge with canary release behind feature flag.
- Phase 4: collect customer-facing VPAT annex and ship with release notes.

Risks and mitigation:
- Virtualized tables make aria-rowindex accurate only if we compute absolute indexes; mitigate by adding an index-offset prop from the virtualization layer.
- Performance regression from additional attribute updates; mitigate by batching DOM writes and testing perf with our runtime harness.

QA steps:
- Run automated axe snapshots for each theme and state; compare diffs to baseline.
- Manual screen reader walkthroughs following the test script in the VPAT annex.
- Keyboard-only navigation smoke tests across Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.

Links to artifacts and references are in attachments.
